newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Seagate sees "very good" disk drive demand in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Seagate sees "very good" disk drive demand in 1997.

text.p: SINGAPORE, January 13 - Seagate Technology Inc expects disk drive demand for use in personal computers and for system servers to be "very good" in 1997, its chairman and chief executive Alan F. Shugart said on Monday.

"Right now we are on allocation just as we were for most of December on our high-performance drives and for most of our desk-top drives...from a disk-drive standpoint, it looks very good," Shugart told a news conference before the official opening of Seagate's mega disc drive facility in Ang Mo Kio.
"My personal opinion is that disk drive demand, both in personal computers and also for enterprise system servers will continue to be good for the rest of calender 1997."
Chief financial officer Donald Waite said the current healthy demand is reflected in the "very severe allocation with all our customers for high performance drives."
Shugart said this was helping to curb the fall in disk drive prices. "Price erosion in the December quarter (October-December 1996) was the lowest that we have seen for a long time."
"That means market demand continues to exceed our ability to rev up production," he said.
Citing analysts' estimates, Waite said the disk drive sector would grow between 18 percent and 25 percent this year, "led obviously by the mobile market."

He said products with mobile computing applications such as notebook computers, handheld data collection devices and cellular phones were the fastest growing market, explaining the current "almost insatiable demand" for high-performance drives.

Ronald Verdoorn, chief operating officer for storage products group, said in the coming months Seagate plans to expand production and its market share of mobile products, an area where it has performed poorly over the past two to three years.
Waite said to meet demand for personal computers and mobile products, Seagate's total capital investment for the current fiscal year (July 1996-June 1997) is just under $1.0 billion.
Seagate, the world's largest independent disk drive maker, said last week that net income rose to $212.6 for the quarter ended December 27, from $148.9 million in the year-ago period.
The company's revenue rose 2.6 percent to $2.4 billion from $2.34 billion a year ago.
Singapore now accounts for more than 55 percent of Seagate's disc drive revenue generation.
Seagate invested $135 million in fixed assets for its new plant, which has a built-up area of one million square feet, bringing its total fixed fixed asset investment in Singapore to $1.1 billion.
The plant was opened on Monday by Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong.
The plant is now producing some of the industry's most technically innovative, high-performance disk drives, including Seagate's Elite 23, a 23.4 gigabyte disk drive.
Shugart said the plant is capable of producing 50,000 high-end disk drives a day from the middle of the year, making it the most productive operation of its kind worldwide.
The company now has 19,400 employees in Singapore, 15,000 of whom would be working in the new facility by the middle of the year, he said.
